meta.title: Altura · The week you set up your own Should
meta.description: Altura is a life reset retreat in Costa Rica's Central Valley. In one week you set up your own Should, a team of AI agents that runs the admin of your life, on your own laptop and around your own goals.

hero.eyebrow: Altura · a life reset retreat · Costa Rica
hero.title: Come for a week. Set up your own Should.
hero.body: Should is a team of AI agents that runs the admin of your life: email, calendar, to-dos, bills and goals. Altura is the week you set up your own, on your own laptop and your own Claude account, in Costa Rica's Central Valley, alongside professionals from around the world. You go home with a setup built around your life, and a network that lasts.
hero.status: Pilot cohort. Dates and price aren't set yet, and signing up commits you to nothing.
hero.imgAlt: Sunset breaking through clouds over the hills of Grecia, in Costa Rica's Central Valley

should.title: What Should does all day
should.body: Should already runs one person's life, every day. It handles the small stuff on its own and brings you only the decisions that are really yours.

points.title: One morning summary
points.body: At 8 AM, in chat: the three things that matter today, what you're waiting on, and anything that needs you. By text too, once you add your own number.

points.title: An agent team for the small stuff
points.body: Agents for money, home, health, career and travel sort the inbox, track bills, file the paperwork and watch prices, so you don't have to remember.

points.title: Only the real decisions reach you
points.body: Anything that spends money, sends a message to someone or can't be undone waits for your yes. You answer with 1, 2 or 3.

points.title: A dashboard for everything
points.body: Every agent has a desk on a private dashboard for your laptop and phone, with your projects and goals beside them.

points.title: It starts from your values
points.body: Your values and goals decide the small calls. A weekly sit-down keeps them current and turns the week into at most three commitments.

day.title: You answer with a number and get on with your day
day.body: Nothing to dig through. Should brings you one thing at a time, in chat, or by text once you add your own number.
day.label: Example conversation

texts.text: Good morning. Today: dentist at 10:30, call Dana back, and the car registration is done. Waiting on: the landlord about the bathroom fan.
One decision: your gym renews at $39 a month on the 1st. 1 renew, 2 switch to the $25 plan, 3 ask me Friday.
Done. The $25 plan starts Dec 1, and it's on your list for Friday's review.

items.title: A working prototype
items.body: Should runs its builder's life every day. It isn't a finished app you download, and it changes every week.

items.title: Set up by hand, with you
items.body: At Altura we build your copy together, step by step, around your accounts and your rules. Expect a few rough edges.

items.title: No promised outcomes
items.body: It can take a lot of small work off your plate. It won't fix your money, health or career for you, and we don't promise income or results.

yours.title: Your life stays on your machine

points.title: On your own laptop
points.body: Your Should runs on your machine, with your own Claude account. Altura never holds your data.

points.title: Your accounts, your access
points.body: You connect the email, calendar and to-do apps you already use, and you choose what each agent may read.

points.title: Rules you write
points.body: Agents ask before money, messages to other people, deletes and settings. You decide what else they ask about.

week.title: From what matters to you, to your own setup
week.body: Mornings are for building, afternoons are for the valley. A draft plan for the pilot, so details will change.

days.title: Arrive
days.body: Pickup at the San José airport, the pool and gardens, a welcome dinner. A quick laptop check so everyone starts ready.

days.title: Values and goals
days.body: A sit-down on what matters to you: your values, what never happens without your yes, what's never shared, and what a good week looks like. Then we lock down your accounts with a password manager, two-factor sign-in and a credit freeze. Dinner ends with a problem swap.

days.title: Connect your accounts
days.body: Claude Code in plain words, then your email, calendar and to-dos connected. The inbox gets cleaned up, everything goes into one list, and your morning summary is scheduled.

days.title: Rest
days.body: Poás volcano at sunrise, hot springs or a slow day. Your first morning summary is waiting wherever you are.

days.title: Choose your agents
days.body: Pick the agents you want first, from money and bills to home and paper mail, and write the rules each one follows.

days.title: Teach them your rules
days.body: Health, career and travel agents, then one-on-one walks with the group. At demo night everyone shows one agent in two minutes.

days.title: Take it home
days.body: Your first weekly review, together, and a 90-day plan. A last security check, then the shuttle to the airport. The cohort chat stays open after you leave.

items.title: A laptop
items.body: With room to install Claude Code and a password manager.

items.title: Your own Claude account
items.body: Pro or Max, which includes Claude Code. It's yours, and you keep it after the week.

items.title: Your phone
items.body: For two-factor codes, and to answer your Should on the go.

items.title: Logins you can reach
items.body: Sign-ins for your email, calendar and to-do app, and your phone for two-factor codes. We send a short checklist before you fly.

items.q: Do I need to know how to code?
items.a: No. You type plain requests to Claude, and we do the setup with you, step by step.
No. Should is a working prototype. At Altura you set up your own copy of the same approach on your own laptop and accounts, and nothing of yours runs on our side.
Dates and price aren't set yet; the pilot list helps us set them. Your Claude plan is separate and paid to Anthropic.
A small group of professionals from different countries and fields. The pilot list helps us shape the group, and you'll know who's coming before you fly.

items.q: I use ChatGPT. Can I still come?
items.a: Should is built on Claude and Claude Code today, so you'll need a Claude Pro or Max account for the week.
Yes. The public demo shows the dashboard with made-up data, and the Should page explains how it works.

people.title: Meet professionals from around the world
people.body: Altura is a small group of professionals from different countries and fields, each building their own Should. The week is built so you get to know them.

items.title: A small, international group
items.body: People from different countries, industries and stages of life, small enough that everyone knows everyone by Tuesday.

items.title: Long dinners and problem swaps
items.body: Evenings are for long-table dinners and swapping problems with people who solve them differently than you do.

items.title: One-on-one walks
items.body: Friday's midday walks pair you with someone new, through the coffee hills.

items.title: A network that lasts
items.body: The cohort chat stays open after the week, so you keep comparing notes, setups and ideas from home.
